era: Arcade / Sega Saturn / Windows / Dreamcast / PlayStation 2
summary: Sega AM2's landmark polygonal light-gun shooter series; use Virtua Cop: Elite Edition on PlayStation 2 for the first two games and arcade hardware/preservation for the arcade-only third game.

primary.version: Virtua Cop: Elite Edition / Virtua Cop Rebirth
primary.why: The PlayStation 2 collection bundles Virtua Cop with Virtua Cop 2 and adds gallery extras plus G-Con 2 light-gun support, making it the most complete documented home route.
primary.how_to_play: Play Virtua Cop: Elite Edition on a PlayStation 2-compatible setup with a supported light gun/display route; use Saturn/Windows/arcade versions for comparison or original-feel preservation.

entries.remaster_caveats: Collection port rather than a full remake; an N-Gage version was developed but canceled and is not counted as a release.

primary.version: Virtua Cop: Elite Edition / Virtua Cop Rebirth
primary.why: Virtua Cop 2 appears in the PlayStation 2 Elite Edition collection with the first game and light-gun support, making it the cleanest complete home package over the older Saturn, Windows, and Dreamcast releases.
primary.how_to_play: Play Virtua Cop: Elite Edition on a PlayStation 2-compatible setup with G-Con 2-compatible controls/display; use Dreamcast or arcade routes only for comparison.

entries.remaster_caveats: Collection port rather than a full remake.

entries.title: Virtua Cop 3

emulation.emulator: Original arcade hardware / Chihiro preservation route
emulation.notes: Arcade cabinet is the reference route.

primary.why: Virtua Cop 3 was released exclusively for arcades on Sega Chihiro hardware; the planned Xbox version was canceled, so the arcade version is the only complete released game.
primary.how_to_play: Play on an original arcade cabinet where possible, or use a legally dumped Chihiro preservation setup if available.

entries.remaster_caveats: The planned Xbox port was canceled, and no modern home version exists.
